head: d85da9a0a9bac345854da0a013956088d7a21f00
claim: a person links a ChatGPT account in their own app and the provider's answer comes back through the installed @byokit/accounts package

steps.start: a fresh consumer app with no package installed and no account linked
steps: install the shipped @byokit/accounts package into the app
the app links a ChatGPT account by device code: it shows a code and the person approves it
the app reads the account status
the app asks the provider a question and prints the answer it gets back
steps.result: the installed package answers: "ChatGPT is connected." and the answer "You said: Plan my day"

steps.start: an app with the previous released @byokit/accounts version installed from the npm registry
steps: the person links a ChatGPT account by device code and gets the provider's answer back
the app upgrades the installed package in place, over the version it had
the person links a ChatGPT account again and gets the provider's answer back through the upgraded package
steps.result: the upgraded package answers: "ChatGPT is connected." and the answer "You said: Plan my day"

verdicts.seen: I read all six lines of the capture. The sign-in line shows a waiting code, and the status line reads 'ChatGPT is connected.' The streamed and answer lines both show 'You said: Plan my day', so the provider's answer came back through @byokit/accounts@0.30.0. The 'not offered' and 'no account' lines are separate negative cases and do not contradict the success path. The provider is the kit's local stand-in rather than real OpenAI, which is the only reason I did not put correct higher. The outcome names a single part, so parts and covers are empty.

Read 3 entries: the 0.29.0 install (step 1), the in-place upgrade (step 2), and the core journey on 0.30.0 (step 3). In step 3 the capture shows 'sign-in: waiting code MOCK-10001', 'status: ChatGPT is connected.', and 'streamed: You said: Plan my day' with 'answer: You said: Plan my day'. The provider's answer comes back through @byokit/accounts@0.30.0, which matches the outcome. The 'not offered' and 'no account' lines are expected negative checks and do not contradict the outcome.
